question_text: According to the course material, capital expenditure is an expenditure incurred by an entity and the benefit of which transcends:
explanation: Capital expenditure benefits more than one year.

question_text: According to the course material, capital expenditure or long-term expenditure is an investment in non-current assets, whether:
explanation: Capex is investment in tangible or intangible non-current assets.

question_text: According to the course material, examples of intangible assets include trademark, patent, copyright, development cost, mineral right, and:
explanation: Intangibles named include mining license.

question_text: According to the course material, assets that generate benefits in more than one accounting period are expensed to the income statement through a process called:
explanation: Capex is expensed via depreciation.

question_text: According to the course material, when capital expenditure on equipment is made you Dr Equipment A/c and Cr:
explanation: Dr Equipment; Cr Cash/Bank.

question_text: According to the course material, when a portion of expenditure on equipment is expensed, you Dr Profit or loss A/c and Cr:
explanation: Depreciation is not credited to the asset account.

question_text: According to the course material, revenue expenditure is incurred in day-to-day running; its benefits expire in the year it is incurred and therefore is charged in whole to:
option_a: the profit or loss A/c in the year of occurrence
explanation: Revenue expenditure is fully charged in the year incurred.

question_text: According to the course material, examples of revenue expenditure are wages and salaries, motor running expenses, electricity, advertising, repairs, travelling and transportation, discounts allowed and:
explanation: Interest expense is listed as revenue expenditure.

question_text: According to the course material, motor vehicle running expense is not a capital expenditure but:
option_a: revenue expenditure and so must be kept separate from acquisition cost of motor vehicle
explanation: Running expenses stay separate from vehicle cost.

question_text: According to the course material, repairs that increase or enhance operating capacity of non-current assets which benefits more than one period will be:
explanation: Capacity-enhancing repairs are capitalised.

question_text: According to the course material, entities encourage sales by selling on credit; without this concession sales would be limited to buyers who can pay:
explanation: Credit sales reach buyers who cannot pay immediately.

question_text: According to the course material, if a 2% discount is offered to a trade debtor for N10,000, the amount expected in full settlement is:
According to the course material, accounting entries for discount allowed are Dr Discount allowed A/c and Cr:
explanation: Dr Discount allowed; Cr receivables.

question_text: According to the course material, the part of the debtors' figure that is not collectible is called:
explanation: Uncollectible trade debts are bad debts.

question_text: According to the course material, when trade debts become bad the accounting entries are Dr Bad debts A/c and Cr:
explanation: Write off: Dr Bad debts; Cr receivables.

question_text: According to the course material, when a previously written-off debt is recovered you Dr Cash/Bank A/c and Cr:
option_b: the old bad debts a/c only as GST
explanation: Recovered bad debts are income, not reopened through bad debts a/c.

question_text: According to the course material, the current conventional accounting term for provision is:
explanation: Provision is now called allowance.

question_text: According to the course material, prudence concept demands that the entity should make allowance for probable uncollectible trade debts; this gives rise to specific allowance and:
explanation: Specific and general allowances for doubtful debts.

question_text: According to the course material, general allowances are usually lower than specific allowances because the level of uncertainty of the former is:
explanation: General allowance rate is usually lower.

question_text: According to the course material, based on accruals and matching concepts, revenues must be matched with expenses used to generate such revenues; it does not matter whether or not:
option_a: cash has been received in relation to the revenues or cash paid in relation to the expenses
explanation: Recognition is on earned/incurred, not cash.

question_text: According to the course material, accrued expenses are expenses incurred in the current accounting period but not yet:
explanation: Accrued expenses = incurred but unpaid.

question_text: According to the course material, if insurance incurred is N20,000 but the firm has paid N17,000 only, the entire N20,000 must be charged to profit or loss and the unpaid N3,000 is:
explanation: Unpaid incurred expense is a current liability.

question_text: According to the course material, prepaid expenses are amounts paid for which the benefits are expected to derive in the future; they have not been incurred because they relate to:
explanation: Prepayments relate to a future period.

question_text: According to the course material, if an entity paid rent of N240,000 for two years, only half of it (N120,000) relates to the current accounting period while the remainder relates to:
explanation: Half is prepaid for next year.

question_text: According to the course material, depreciation is the process of allocating the cost of tangible non-current asset over its estimated useful life as expense to:
explanation: Depreciation allocates cost to the income statement.
